triggerReason: Redundant deployment-mode labels competed with city information, non-Observatory views lacked the intended cyberpunk atmosphere, and the existing theme selector did not provide a real light palette.
action: Removed observer-mode and software-run badges from rendered UI; replaced dark, hacker and matrix settings with persistent light and dark palettes; migrated old theme values safely; kept Human Observatory restrained while adding a shared multicolor cyberpunk atmosphere to every other view; added desktop/mobile WCAG checks for both modes.
outcome: Implementation 355bec9 darkens light-theme blue and green semantics, prevents pre-hydration theme races, and expands the Observatory light-mode axe gate. It passed 245 tests with real PostgreSQL and independent restore coverage, 26 Playwright/axe scenarios, three repeated theme migrations, zero TypeScript or lint warnings, zero audit vulnerabilities, the production build, exact 365-Turn replay, the v2 closure gate and the 12-case model regression. Tag v4.3.2 at c36f542 is deployed; production Chromium found zero WCAG A/AA violations, overflow, console errors or removed labels across desktop/mobile Observatory and Dashboard in both modes. The existing season continued through Turn 15 with resource conservation and zero severe escapes.
evidence: Light and dark palettes use semantic CSS variables
Persisted hacker and matrix values normalize to dark
Human Observatory does not render cyberpunk background effects
Every other view inherits the shared cyberpunk shell
Redundant English and Chinese status labels are absent from rendered UI
Desktop and mobile light/dark palettes have zero WCAG A/AA violations and no horizontal overflow
All primary views render inside the cyberpunk shell without application or console errors
The production audit, not the release claim, is authoritative when dynamic data reveals a missed contrast state
